title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval & Regression Checks
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality evals and regressions on the prompt sets for Zenith Retail's customer support assistant. Reviewed scoring results, discussed false positives on content filters, proposed tuning to prompts and post-processing, and agreed next steps for a focused A/B on two prompt variants and a benchmark run on dedicated nodes.
next_steps: Redwood: share detailed scoring spreadsheet and prompts by 2026-03-20
Zenith: run the two prompt variants on 1 week of live traffic (shadow) and provide logs by 2026-03-25
Schedule dedicated-node benchmark with Redwood SE week of 2026-03-23
Security: Redwood to share SOC2 + KMS design doc by 2026-03-22
action_items: Maya Chen - Share scoring spreadsheet and current prompt CSV - 2026-03-20
Diego Alvarez - Prepare benchmark run plan and resource estimate for dedicated nodes - 2026-03-22
Tom Reynolds - Provide 1-week anonymized sample of customer support transcripts for A/B shadowing - 2026-03-20

transcript:
Header: 2026-03-18 15:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor, Tom Reynolds, Sara Li, Michael Owens, Jordan Park

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync focusing on quality evaluation and regression checks across prompt sets and scoring; discussed guardrails and next steps.

00:00 Priya Kapoor: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. We're about four weeks into the pilot, excited to see where the quality metrics landed.
00:12 Maya Chen: Great, Priya - thanks. Quick agenda: go over the scoring spreadsheet, highlight regressions, talk prompt variants and guardrails, then next steps. Diego will walk through the benchmark plan.
00:32 Diego Alvarez: Hi all. So for context, we ran the current prompt set across the evaluation harness you sent, plus about 2k live-ish samples from last week. Scoring rubric: helpfulness, relevance, and hallucination rate. We normalized scores 0-100.
00:55 Tom Reynolds: Quick note - our anonymization script removed PII, but some entity names still look weird in transcript, so scores may be slightly skewed.
01:10 Diego Alvarez: Yep noted. Overall numbers: avg helpfulness 78, relevance 84, hallucination 9%. That's improvement from last week on helpfulness, small regression on hallucination for the returns flow.
01:35 Priya Kapoor: Returns flow? That's a high-risk path for us, especially legal. Can you surface a few examples?
01:47 Diego Alvarez: Sure. I'll read a couple snippets - these are paraphrased. Example A: user asks about returning a faulty blender and the model suggests contacting a third-party repair center, which is not in our policy. That's counted as a hallucination / policy miss.
02:12 Sara Li: We saw that too in production logs, a handful of cases where the model invented policy. That's concerning.
02:25 Maya Chen: Understood. Two levers here: prompt-level guardrails (explicit disallow statements plus preferred response templates) and post-processing filters that rewrite or block disallowed suggestions. We recommend adding a short policy fragment in the system prompt for returns flow.
02:48 Tom Reynolds: If we add policy text to the prompt, will that increase latency or cost? We worry about token count.
03:00 Diego Alvarez: It adds tokens but small delta; biggest impact is if you push longer context or history. We can also move some checks to the microservice layer post-response to avoid token bloat.
03:20 Michael Owens: From infosec, any PII leakage concerns with the prompt additions? Also, what about encryption of logs? Are KV cache dumps obfuscated?
03:35 Maya Chen: Good questions. Redwood stores evaluation logs encrypted at rest; for Private deployments you control KMS, and for Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys. For hosted, we have server-side KMS and can provide redaction hooks. Diego, feel free to add the SOC2 stuff.
03:48 Diego Alvarez: Right - we are SOC2 Type II, we can share the report under NDA. KV cache is never logged by default; we only log request/response and meta. Customers can opt-in for more granular logs with masking.
04:10 Priya Kapoor: Okay, that helps. Back to scoring - can you show the regression comparison across last three runs?
04:22 Diego Alvarez: Yep. (screen) Last three weekly runs: hallucination for returns: 3% -> 7% -> 9%. We traced the uplift to a prompt change on 02/28 where we relaxed a constraint to be more helpful in edge cases. That increased helpfulness but opened hallucination.
04:48 Sara Li: So it's a tradeoff. We prefer fewer hallucinations even if helpfulness dips slightly. Customer trust matters more.
04:56 Maya Chen: Good to know. Let's A/B test two variants: V1 (conservative): explicit safety template + shorter answer constraints; V2 (helpful): current plus clarifying question logic. Run as shadow for one week over live traffic subset.
05:15 Priya Kapoor: Sounds good; what's the rollout mechanism? Dedicated vs hosted?
05:22 Diego Alvarez: For the POC we can run both on hosted nodes to iterate fast. If you want to assess tail latency and determinism on dedicated, we schedule a benchmark on dedicated nodes - Diego will own that. For production, dedicated is recommended for throughput and SLA.
05:45 Jordan Park: Will shadowing add cost? We have to estimate infra costs.
05:51 Maya Chen: Shadowing doesn't double your billed inference for hosted - you can sample. We can provide a cost estimate; Diego will include it in the benchmark plan.
06:05 Tom Reynolds: On scoring rubrics - we noticed annotator variance on 'helpfulness' labels. Can Redwood help tune thresholds or provide calibration?
06:16 Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can run calibration using the same rater pool or apply automatic heuristics to normalize. We'll also supply the raw annotator-level data so you can see variance.
06:30 Priya Kapoor: Guardrails again - for the returns flow could we implement a quick blacklist of disallowed suggestions? e.g., "do not recommend third-party repair"?
06:43 Maya Chen: Absolutely. Two options: static blacklist in post-processing or soft-block in prompt. Static blacklist is deterministic and safe. Soft-block is more flexible but needs careful prompt engineering.
06:58 Michael Owens: For security sign-off we need the audit trail of any post-processing decisions. Is that feasible?
07:06 Diego Alvarez: We can emit audit events for each blocked/rewritten response with reason codes. Those events can be sent to your SIEM. We'll include schema in the SOC2 package.
07:25 Sara Li: About metrics dashboards - can Redwood break down metrics by route, model variant, and prompt version? We want to see per-flow performance.
07:34 Maya Chen: Yes, Console has per-route and per-model dashboards; we can add a custom tag for prompt version and surface regression alerts when metrics cross thresholds.
07:48 Priya Kapoor: Great. On the hands-on side, Diego, can you outline the benchmark plan?
07:55 Diego Alvarez: Plan: 1) baseline run on hosted with sample workload; 2) dedicated-node run (1x and 2x capacity) to measure 99th p50/p95 latency and throughput; 3) quality run with A/B prompt variants on shadow traffic; 4) cost projection using token counts and batching profiles. Expected time: 3-4 days of runs, plus analysis. We estimate dedicated run cost ~ $X (placeholder) - will provide number.
08:28 Tom Reynolds: For the dedicated run, do you support GPU types? We prefer A100 or H100.
08:33 Diego Alvarez: We support both, and we pick kernels per model. We'll include hardware mapping in the plan.
08:41 Priya Kapoor: One more from product: we saw occasional hallucinations in the knowledge base responses where the model incorrectly merged two articles. Any suggestions?
08:56 Maya Chen: That's often a retrieval or prompt concatenation issue. Two fixes: improve retrieval precision / rerank or provide strict templates to avoid merging. Also consider chunking long docs.
09:12 Sara Li: OK. Quick question about the evaluation harness - can you add a guardrail-specific test set that focuses on returns and billing flows?
09:20 Diego Alvarez: Yes, please send canonical examples; we'll create a targeted eval and run nightly.
09:28 Priya Kapoor: Logistics: we'll send the sample transcripts and canonical cases by Friday.
09:34 Maya Chen: Recap of action items: Maya to send scoring spreadsheet, Diego to prepare benchmark run plan and costs, Tom to send anonymized transcripts, Michael to review SOC2 docs. We'll target the A/B shadow start next Monday if inputs land on time.
09:53 Tom Reynolds: One small nit - sometimes the transcript engine tags the SE as Speaker 1; don't worry about names in the logs.
10:02 Maya Chen: Noted. Any other blockers?
10:06 Michael Owens: No blockers; we just need the SOC2 artifacts and the KMS design for our legal review.
10:12 Priya Kapoor: Thanks everyone. End of meeting.
